intent: Check Agent updates on startup, hourly, and explicit user request while eliminating unchanged update telemetry writes and their dependent security-rule reads; also resume only the registered Android Agent and user-enabled Control Add-On automatically after device boot while keeping the Android Viewer manual.

requestReview.reason: Windows Agent update checks now run at startup and on the one-hour scheduler itself instead of waking every minute. The signed manifest is HTTP-hosted; an unchanged successful result no longer writes transient checking/healthy telemetry to the device document, preventing those writes from repeatedly reevaluating the command listener's device-dependent rule. Android boot hardening adds no recurring request. Request-time screen approval adds one bounded local notification timer per explicit Viewer connection command and no polling or additional cloud request.
requestReview.assumptions: Scoped Firestore delta, NOT total fleet billing: one registered Windows Agent runs for 24h on the current release with successful signed-manifest responses, no manual update click, update transition, failure, process restart, command, remote session or listener reconnect. It performs one startup plus 24 hourly HTTP manifest checks. Those 25 unchanged checks produce zero Firestore update-telemetry reads and writes. Initial registration/authentication, one startup presence write, the command listener's initial query and rule dependencies, software manifest HTTP traffic, manual presence refreshes, actual updates/failures, Viewer traffic and SDK reconnects remain separate nonzero traffic. A changed update state is intentionally written once; no production billing measurement is claimed.

checks.idle: Actual Agent watch-block execution with fake time performs exactly 24 update calls and zero heartbeats over 24h. Poll policy separately proves the first check is immediately eligible. Transient checking plus unchanged healthy telemetry produces no report call.
checks.rerender: Agent active UI has one button handler and no React effect for update polling; the child Agent process alone owns the automatic scheduler. Opening or rerendering the UI therefore does not add a periodic check.
checks.concurrency: The existing Agent isUpdating gate prevents overlapping automatic checks. The UI disables repeated clicks while the native checker is running, and the existing updater owns its handoff lifecycle.
checks.failure: A real failed state still produces exactly one telemetry report and the UI surfaces native check/install errors. Hourly automatic attempts and explicit manual checks remain available; unchanged recovery state is deduplicated after it is reported.
checks.cleanup: The automatic interval belongs to the Agent child process and ends with it. The one-shot native checker waits for its hidden child and returns one parsed result. No new listener, service, retry timer or persistent UI subscription was added.

rollback: Keep unrelated edits and prior auxiliary-queue quota fixes. Roll back manual-presence Agent behavior and connection freshness policy together if necessary; never restore strict heartbeat aging while deployed Agents have no heartbeat timer. Deploy matching Firestore rules and Functions before releasing manual-presence Agents. Restoring recurring list/heartbeat traffic would reintroduce quota waste and needs explicit review. For the Android auto-start addition, remove only the Control Add-On direct-boot declaration and its focused tests.

outcomes.acceptance: The registered desktop Agent checks for signed updates once at startup, then once per hour, and exposes an Update check button that reports current/error state or confirms an available update before using the existing installer updater. An unchanged successful check produces no Firestore telemetry write; update transitions and failures remain visible.
boundaries: Firestore update telemetry and dependent command listener rules
outcomes.verification: 2026-09-05: npx vitest run src/agent/agentUpdatePollPolicy.test.ts src/agent/agentPresence.test.ts passed 9 tests after RED failures for the old 15-minute default, one-minute scheduler and absent telemetry deduplication. The actual watch block makes 24 calls/24h and zero heartbeats; transient plus unchanged healthy state causes no report, while a failure reports once. Focused desktopPackaging native-update contract passed 1 test with 61 unrelated cases skipped. npx tsc --noEmit and cargo check --lib passed. Rust formatting check remains globally red on extensive pre-existing formatting differences and is not claimed as passing.
outcomes.physicalGap: No build/deployment requested. Installed Agent button, hourly wall clock, updater handoff and live Firestore billing require later release/device verification.

outcomes.acceptance: Viewer login and idle time do not load device/history data. Refresh explicitly reads them and requests a bounded status response from registered Agents. Windows and Android Agents no longer send timer-driven heartbeats; command reception and automatic software updates remain available. Old heartbeat age alone must not permanently prevent an explicit authorized remote connection.
boundaries: Windows Agent command and update lifecycle

outcomes.acceptance: Remote connections start only from Connect. Failed/disconnected sessions do not run automatic reconnect loops, including reboot recovery; the session refresh button performs one explicit reconnect attempt and cleanup prevents late work.
outcomes.verification: 2026-09-05: src/viewerDeviceRefresh.test.ts passed in the 129-test focused run. Real Chromium StrictMode starts one transport per explicit Connect, makes zero automatic restarts over 24h after failure, and starts one replacement from the session refresh icon. Reboot timers were removed along with the automatic failure scheduler; cleanup closes late transports. Signaling is mocked, so this is UI lifecycle proof, not physical remote recovery.
outcomes.physicalGap: Physical Android/Windows reconnects are not exercised by mocked signaling; user explicitly chose manual reconnect over previous automatic recovery.

outcomes.acceptance: An idle connected Viewer and Windows Agent issue no recurring chat/clipboard/file/receipt queries. New events still reach the intended receiver once, unused receipt monitoring is absent, slow handlers are serialized, and session stop prevents late delivery. Firebase and local API paths preserve these behaviors; Android heartbeat/signaling are not replaced by polling.

outcomes.physicalGap: No build/deployment requested. Installed Windows/Android behavior, physical clipboard/file delivery and metered production usage require later device verification. Heartbeat scheduling is superseded by refresh-only-presence-and-lists; event-driven presence, update checks and essential local capture/command transport remain.

outcomes.acceptance: Desktop and mobile shared Viewer UI loads devices only on explicit refresh, not login; no idle list reads or automatic online/offline transitions. This supersedes the earlier login-plus-refresh acceptance. Cached offline entries can initiate normal, secure and split requests; backend ownership, stored offline status and protocol checks remain, with heartbeat aging retained for legacy Agents only.

outcomes.acceptance: Completion and future commit checks reject missing request reviews; request-affecting changes must declare a bounded daily budget, lifecycle evidence, and a changed request-boundary test. History regression checks cover an idle day without polling, while post-deployment proof-only edits validate the committed release boundary instead of unrelated workspace files.
outcomes.verification: 2026-09-05: npx vitest run scripts/verify-recurrence-coverage.test.js passed 14 tests. Missing review and lifecycle/budget guards fail, untracked workspace files cannot replace committed release boundaries, post-deployment proof-only edits reuse the committed boundary set, and actual code edits remain restricted to their current changed files. Earlier history checks passed 24h idle and unsubscribe request-count scenarios. Tests are offline and do not prove aggregate production usage.
outcomes.physicalGap: The gate validates review completeness and stated budgets, not the truth of unmeasured fleet assumptions. Existing request paths beyond the history subscription require a separate audit.

outcomes.acceptance: Registration reports a server quota failure accurately without saving a false registration; Agent retries are delayed while quota is exhausted and registration succeeds after quota recovery.
outcomes.verification: Live read-only Firestore probe returned HTTP 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; billingEnabled=false and freeTier=true. :agent:testDebugUnitTest --tests com.wonremote.agent.FirebaseQuotaTest passed 2 tests with the real Firebase exception class and test-only Android container/string fixtures; Agent debug Java compilation passed. Registration persistence remains after successful transaction completion only. This does not prove physical registration recovery.
outcomes.physicalGap: Production Firestore currently returns HTTP 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED. Quota recovery and Android registration after a future requested build must be verified; no billing changes are authorized.

outcomes.acceptance: Superseding the earlier stable-listener policy, Firebase and local Viewer history now query only on explicit history refresh, never mount or a timer. Firebase uses a server-only bounded session query and existing device metadata; there is no UI history subscription.
outcomes.verification: npx vitest run src/firebase/viewerConnectionHistory.test.ts src/firebase/firebaseSecurityPolicy.test.ts src/api/viewerApi.test.ts passed 32 tests; new history regressions failed before implementation. Fake-time runtime tests cover an idle hour without repeated queries, updated session metadata, quota error, unsubscribe and explicit retry. UI routing is covered by a source contract, not a browser/device E2E. npx tsc --noEmit passed.
outcomes.physicalGap: Live usage reduction requires deployment and closing or updating old polling Viewers. No build or deployment requested this turn.

outcomes.acceptance: After one-time Agent registration and one-time Control Add-On accessibility approval, a device reboot resumes the Agent connection service and rebinds the Add-On input service without opening either app UI; the Android Viewer never auto-starts and screen sharing still requires Android user approval.
outcomes.verification: 2026-09-05: BootReceiverTest passed 1 focused Android unit test for registered-only BOOT_COMPLETED, QUICKBOOT_POWERON and MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED handling. The focused desktopPackaging Vitest failed RED before the Add-On declaration and then passed 1 test with 62 unrelated cases skipped, proving Agent-only boot reception, no projection auto-start and no Viewer boot receiver. :controladdon:processDebugManifest passed and its final merged manifest contains android:directBootAware=true. No APK build was requested or run.
outcomes.physicalGap: A real reboot is required to verify OEM battery policy, foreground notification delivery, persisted accessibility approval and service rebinding. MediaProjection cannot be auto-approved by this path.

outcomes.acceptance: When the background Android Agent receives an explicit Viewer start-stream request without an active projection, it raises one high-priority approval notification. Tapping it opens the Agent and Android full-display consent dialog; approval starts the pending session, while rejection, expiry or session closure removes the request and projection. No screen capture starts at boot or without user consent.
outcomes.verification: 2026-09-05: AgentProjectionRequestTest and BootReceiverTest passed 2 focused Android unit tests after the request-policy test failed RED. The Android task compiled Agent Java and processed the manifest. Focused desktopPackaging Vitest passed 2 request-time approval and boot-autostart contracts after failing RED on the missing singleTop launch path. No APK build was requested or run.
outcomes.physicalGap: A physical Android device must confirm heads-up notification visibility over the table-order app, notification permission behavior, system consent UI, accepted stream startup and reject/timeout cleanup.
